lesson.title: Mass Atrocities After 1900
lesson.summary: How governments and armed groups carried out genocide and mass killing in the twentieth century, including the Holocaust.
learningGoals: Explain the various causes and consequences of mass atrocities from 1900 to the present.
lesson.bigIdea: In the twentieth century, governments and armed movements used propaganda, state power, and modern organization to carry out genocide and mass killing.
lesson.context: Genocide means acts committed with intent to destroy a national, ethnic, racial, or religious group. The word was coined in 1944.

sections.title: The Holocaust

blocks.text: The Nazi regime stripped Jews of their rights through laws such as the Nuremberg Laws of 1935. During the war, the Nazis carried out the systematic murder of about six million Jews in the Holocaust, as well as Roma, disabled people, and others.

blocks.title: Cause and effect
blocks.text: Racist ideology, propaganda, and the power of a modern state allowed persecution to become organized mass murder.

sections.takeaway: The Holocaust was a state-organized genocide driven by racist ideology.

sections.title: Other mass atrocities

blocks.text: During World War I, the Ottoman government deported and killed a large share of its Armenian population in the Armenian genocide, beginning in 1915. The Khmer Rouge regime in Cambodia caused the deaths of 1.5 to 2 million people from 1975 to 1979. In Rwanda in 1994, Hutu extremists killed an estimated 500,000 to 800,000 people, mostly Tutsi, in about one hundred days.

blocks.title: Common trap
blocks.text: Atrocities were not spontaneous. Strong answers identify the role of governments, organized groups, and propaganda.

sections.takeaway: Mass atrocities occurred across the century and the world.

vocabulary.definition: Acts committed with intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnic, racial, or religious group.
The Nazi genocide of about six million Jews during World War II.
The deportation and killing of Armenians by the Ottoman government beginning in 1915.

connections.title: Human rights after 1945
connections.body: The horrors of the Holocaust led to the 1948 Genocide Convention and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, studied in Unit 9.
connections.transferQuestion: How did the Holocaust shape international law after 1945?
connections.feedback: Name a specific agreement and explain the connection.
